_readme: Meaning of the filter categories and of the values that need it, for the AI search (step 'understand': the AI maps the user's words to the tags).
They describe what a category or value means, not what a single project achieved.
Values of D1-D6 are described in nbsDefinitions.json (the same texts shown in the case card): not repeated here.
Values not listed have no description: their name is clear enough, or their meaning is not certain (see 'not_described').

source: authors_excel = section headings of the authors' Excel template; data_thresholds = thresholds measured on the cases (data-source/REPORT-DATI.md 3.5); draft = written for the AI search and checked against the cases that have the tag.
status: approved = confirmed by the TALEA team; draft = to be reviewed by the TALEA team. Change status to approved after review, and the version date after any change.

talea_application.text: TALEA green cells application: how the intervention is laid out in space; several can apply

size.text: area of the project: Small < ~0.2 ha; Medium ~0.2-5 ha; Large >= 5 ha, or a corridor >= 1 km, or a city-wide programme

climate_zone.text: climate of the project's location (main climate groups; Mediterranean = mild wet winters and hot dry summers, listed apart from Temperate)

a1_urban_scale.text: A Physical characteristics. Urban scale (relevance): the scale at which the project matters, i.e. its area of influence, not its physical size; from Territorial (beyond the city) and Metropolitan, to Urban (the whole city), District, Urban block and Single space or building; several can apply

a2_urban_area.text: Urban area (location): where the project is in the city

a3_1_buildings.text: Type of space transformed: buildings or parts of buildings

a3_2_open_spaces.text: Type of space transformed: open spaces

a3_3_infrastructures.text: Type of space transformed: mobility and water infrastructures

a6_uses.text: activities and uses the space hosts

b1_physical.text: B Constraints and opportunities: conditions of the site and its context that the project had to deal with or could build on (a B tag documents a condition, not a result). Physical constraints of the site

b2_regulations.text: Constraints: rules and legal limits the project had to respect

b3_uses_management.text: Constraints and opportunities from uses, management, signage and equipment already on or around the site

b4_public_opinion.text: Constraints and opportunities from public opinion: attitudes of residents and users towards the place

b5_synergy.text: Opportunities: synergy with other projects or programmes in the area (plans, regeneration projects, investments)

b6_social_opportunities.text: Social opportunities the project could build on or develop (a potential, not a measured result)

c1_1_design.text: C Design process, stakeholders, integrated services and outcomes. Design process: how the project was designed and with whom

c1_3_management.text: Process: how the space is managed after the works

c2_actors.text: Actors involved: people and organisations that took part in the project

c3_goals.text: Goals and results: aims stated by the project. A goal does not prove that the benefit was achieved or measured (measured effects, if any, are in the C5 impacts text of the card)

c4_services.text: Other integrated services offered to the users of the space

d1_plants.text: D Nature-based solutions built in the project: plants

d3_water.text: Nature-based solutions: water and stormwater management

d4_roof_facade.text: Nature-based solutions: green roofs and facades

d6_urban_spaces.text: Nature-based solutions: types of green urban space

innovation.text: what is new in the project: Physical (spaces, materials, techniques), Social (participation, management, new uses), Digital (sensors, apps, data)

Nodal.text: a single place: a square, courtyard, building or park

Linear.text: along a line: a street, corridor, canal, riverbank or barrier

Fragmented.text: several separate small interventions spread over an area (called Diffuse in the authors' template)

Consolidated city.text: the established built-up fabric, outside the historical centre

Residual space or widening.text: leftover space without a defined function, or a small widening along a street

Service yard or technical area.text: yard for services, deliveries or technical equipment

Temporary use.text: uses for a limited time, e.g. interim or tactical uses

In-between space.text: space between buildings, blocks or functions, often without a clear role

Neighbourhood space.text: everyday space of a neighbourhood, used mainly by local residents

Consolidated use / uses.text: established uses of the space that had to be kept or taken into account

Green/blue infrastructure.text: existing green or water elements on or near the site

Maintenance assigned to third parties.text: maintenance entrusted to someone other than the owner (a company, association or residents)

Use conflicts.text: competing uses of the same space, e.g. traffic, parking, play, events

Vulnerable or sensitive users.text: users needing special attention, e.g. children, older people, people with disabilities

Perception of the space as \"private\".text: people felt the space was not open to them

Co-design.text: designed together with residents or users

Public consultation.text: residents asked for their opinion on a proposal

Community engagement.text: the community involved in activities around the project

Research project.text: designed or tested within a research project, e.g. an EU-funded programme

Spontaneous intervention.text: started by citizens on their own initiative, without a formal plan

Self-build.text: built by users or volunteers themselves

Partnership.text: funded jointly by several partners, e.g. public and private

Collaboration agreement.text: managed through a formal agreement between the administration and citizens, associations or private actors (e.g. collaboration pacts)

Age groups.text: specific age groups, e.g. children or older people

Facilitators.text: professionals who run the participation activities

Re-activation.text: bringing an unused or underused space back into use

Re-appropriation.text: residents taking back a space as their own

Valorisation.text: enhancing the value of a place, its landscape or its heritage

New perception.text: changing how people see and experience the place

Monitoring and warning systems.text: systems that measure conditions (e.g. temperature, air, water) or warn of risks

not_described._why: Meaning not certain from the name or from the cases that have the tag: to be described by the TALEA team.
